newsitem.title: SPAIN: Peseta softens under intervention shadow.
newsitem.headline: Peseta softens under intervention shadow.

text.p: The peseta shrugged off a powering dollar against the mark and other currencies as expectations of possible intervention continued to plague the Spanish currency, dealers said on Monday.

With the Bank of Spain hovering in the background, the peseta weakened slightly to 84.35/37 per mark by 0900 GMT, compared with 84.25/27 late on Thursday night. Spanish markets were closed on Friday for a public holiday.
Dealers said the central bank had intervened last week, buying marks at the 84.15/20 per mark level to take any steam out of the peseta.
"We've been trading in a narrow band of between 84.40 and 84.60 for the past three months, so a move to 84.15 prompted action from the central bank," said one dealer.
"In the past it has waited until 84.00 but now it's being cautious," the dealer added.
Traders believe the Bank of Spain is keen to hold the peseta in a band between 84.00 and 85.00 per mark in the run-up to European monetary union.
But analysts say expectations the Bank of Spain is unlikely to cut interest rates soon could put pressure on the peseta to appreciate.
Howver, a surging dollar has exerted little pressure on the currency to strengthen, dealers said.
"If the dollar goes to 1.90 per mark, we may see the peseta under pressure to appreciate," said one dealer. "But for now the dollar strength is not having much effect on the peseta."
The dollar hit seven-and-a-half year highs against the mark overnight at 1.8470, the strongest it has been since November 1989 when it reached 1.8690.
Dealers expect further rallying amid expectations the Bundesbank will not act anytime soon to curb mark weakness.
